evals.prompt: Make this existing dashboard work well from narrow mobile browser widths through large desktop screens without changing its product behavior.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering activates, inspects existing design, and reasons about responsive/adaptive layout and input behavior.

evals.prompt: Use ui-engineering to refine this desktop settings page while preserving our existing DESIGN.md.
evals.expected_output: The project design system remains authoritative and refinement stays proportional.

evals.prompt: A queue consumer duplicates jobs after retry; find the root cause.
Design a WebView checkout screen where native owns authentication and deep links but web owns navigation inside checkout.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering makes the native/web ownership boundary explicit and reports supporting integration/security concerns where relevant.

evals.prompt: Impeccable is installed, but DESIGN.md requires subtle dense desktop UI. Improve typography and spacing.
evals.expected_output: The provider may be composed for typography/layout but DESIGN.md remains authoritative and no new visual direction is invented.

evals.prompt: Review a track actions menu that works with mouse but cannot be opened from keyboard.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering treats keyboard accessibility as product behavior and verifies the relevant interaction.

evals.prompt: Use ui-engineering for a new responsive web product with no component library or CSS strategy selected yet. It needs custom visual identity, dark mode, dialogs, menus, forms, keyboard accessibility, and touch support.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering compares custom, headless-primitives, styled-library, and hybrid strategies against the product's design/accessibility needs instead of defaulting to a popular library. It distinguishes any pervasive architecture-level choice from reversible package details.

evals.prompt: Build the UI foundation for a new app. Tailwind and a shadcn-style library are popular but the project has not selected them.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering does not adopt Tailwind or a component library by popularity/default. It derives component and styling strategy from product/design requirements and existing DESIGN.md truth.

evals.prompt: The product needs custom visual styling but several complex dialogs, menus, popovers, and comboboxes with strong keyboard and screen-reader behavior.
evals.expected_output: ui-engineering seriously considers maintained headless/accessibility primitives to reduce interaction risk while keeping the visual language project-owned; it does not insist on hand-rolling all primitives or importing a full styled system.

evals.prompt: Verify login/register interaction in Zaiko: Svelte SSR renders enabled forms with method=POST. The route uses a client handler to submit to FastAPI, with no native POST action on the frontend route. Svelte type checks and the build pass. A browser can delay JavaScript and inspect the first rendered form. Assess the interaction claim.
evals.expected_output: Directly inspects and exercises the rendered pre-hydration surface, including native submission and handler activation. Detects the POST risk before the client handler is active and does not accept static build/type success as interaction proof. Reports the observed mismatch and needed fix; verifies initial and hydrated states after repair only when authorized.

evals.prompt: Verify an inventory editor. The parent refreshes server data on window focus. The child initializes its editable quantity and revision from props once. A second tab changes the item before focus returns; the backend rejects stale revisions correctly. Static checks pass. Evaluate what the user sees and submits without inventing a draft-discard policy.
evals.expected_output: Exercises focus refresh with an existing draft, inspecting rendered quantity and submitted revision. Identifies stale child state despite server conflict protection; preserves unresolved draft/reconciliation choices for the workflow owner and does not silently overwrite user edits or claim correctness from static checks.

evals.prompt: Refine the rendered household inventory page for quick everyday checks on phone and desktop. Almost every section is a similar bordered card, repeated eyebrow labels precede each heading, explanatory paragraphs compete with item rows, and invite/settings/add-item actions have equal emphasis. CSS validation passes and DESIGN.md has no universal card prohibition. Inspect the available rendered page.
evals.expected_output: Uses rendered inspection and product purpose to critique hierarchy, competing actions, repetitive card/meta treatment, copy, and mobile behavior. Makes proportionate refinements that improve the household task; does not treat CSS validity as visual quality or impose a universal anti-card aesthetic.

evals.prompt: Verify a client-only desktop settings editor with no SSR/hydration. The rendered window and keyboard interaction are available. Checks include save feedback and resizing; static checks pass.
evals.expected_output: Verifies actual rendered save feedback, keyboard behavior, and relevant window sizes. Does not add hydration analysis to a client-only surface or rely solely on static checks.

evals.prompt: Refine a UI layout while the environment exposes source, type checking, and build commands but cannot launch or inspect a browser/device/rendered surface. Report what can be verified here.
evals.expected_output: Uses available static evidence for its supported claims and explicitly leaves visual/runtime interaction verification incomplete. Does not fabricate rendered inspection or mark interaction correctness proved.
